_meta.verification_required: Every dollar amount below must be checked against its IRS publication or revenue procedure. The RULES that consume them (tax_wrappers.py, tax_debt_interest.py) are statutory structure and do not need annual re-verification; these amounts do.
_meta.why_split_from_tax_tables: Deliberate separation. tax_tables holds rate SCHEDULES; this holds the thresholds that statutory RULES test against. The rules are stable across years and encodable with high confidence; these numbers are not. Keeping them apart lets a determination be correct about the rule while explicit that the limit is unverified.
_meta.source: UNVERIFIED — populate from Pub 969 (HSA/HDHP/FSA), Notice 2023-75 (retirement limits), Pub 936 (mortgage interest), Pub 550 (investment interest), Pub 970 (student loan interest), Pub 925 (passive activity)

sources.retirement.uniform_lifetime_table: IRS Publication 590-B (2025), Appendix B Table III (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/p590b.pdf), retrieved 2026-10-12. Life-expectancy tables were last revised effective 2022-01-01 and are NOT annually indexed.

retirement.uniform_lifetime_table_note: IRS Pub 590-B Appendix B, Table III (Uniform Lifetime) — the applicable denominator for an RMD. For unmarried owners, married owners whose spouse is not more than 10 years younger, and married owners whose spouse is not the sole beneficiary. Age 120 is '120 and over'. A spouse MORE than 10 years younger and sole beneficiary uses Table II (Joint and Last Survivor), which is not modelled — it gives a LONGER period and therefore a SMALLER RMD, so using this table for them overstates the forced distribution.
